newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Two people killed in violence in Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Two people killed in violence in Karachi.

text.p: Two people, one of them a member of the Christian minority, were killed in violence overnight in Pakistan's troubled port city of Karachi, police said on Saturday.
They said body of Mark Lazruf, a Christian, was found stuffed in a sack in the Korangi area, while the body of an unidentified youngster was found in Orangi town with his throat slit.
The political affiliations of the victims were not immediately known.

"It is not necessary that these killings are linked with the on-going political violence," Deputy Inspector General of Karachi Police Mohammad Iqbal told Reuters. "They might have been killed in personal disputes... We are investigating the cases."
On Friday, a worker of the ruling Pakistan Muslim League was shot dead in the volatile Baldia area of Karachi. No group has claimed the responsibility for the murder.
Violence surged in Karachi after five Mohajir National Movement (MQM) workers were killed on Monday, closing the main business and commercial centers of the city for three days.
Fighting between the Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and the splinter MQM-Haqiqi faction has claimed more than 50 lives since February 3 elections.
The MQM, which is part of the Sindh province coalition government, represents Urdu-speaking people who migrated from India to Partition in 1947 and their descendents.
More than 100 people have been killed in political and sectarian violence in Karachi this year, compared to 500 in 1996 and more than 2,000 in 1995.
